answer: Because the entropy is measured at the thread gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the zephyr audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 3 bits per word is rejected before grading, as it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. A farm emitting 76 variations of one paragraph therefore burns for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the vine panel. That is 13 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
